description: Add a daily stage-population snapshot mechanism (isolated persistence + daily background job + shared attribution) and a stacked-area Cumulative Flow Diagram (CFD) widget in the Dashboard Productivity zone, fed by an additive project-scoped read endpoint over a fixed trailing window.

tasks.title: Stage-population snapshot mechanism: storage + shared attribution + daily job
tasks.description: Extract the latest-attempt / latest-run-wins / invalidate-on-restart attribution core out of IssueQuerier.ComputeLatestAttemptStageDurations into a shared pure function (time-bounded event stream + ordered stage set -> single attributed stage), and wire both the stage-duration surface and the new snapshot onto it so they cannot diverge. Add an isolated StagePopulationSnapshotRow table (one row per project+day, six int count columns, Day stored as 'yyyy-MM-dd' string, unique (ProjectId, Day) index) with its EF migration and DbSet. Implement StagePopulationSnapshotService : BackgroundService mirroring IssueWorkflowReconciliationService (IOptions period, sweep-swallow exceptions, keyset project walk) with a public SnapshotOnceAsync test seam, deriving each in-flow issue's stage as of the UTC day and writing one idempotent upsert row per project per day. Register via AddHostedService. Cancelled exclusion must read the emitted IssueClosed (com.mohist.issue.closed) event, not the unemitted catalogue entry; day bounds applied in LINQ-to-objects after materialization.
acceptanceCriteria: A new isolated StagePopulationSnapshotRow table + DbSet + migration exists, touching no existing table; unique index UQ_StagePopulationSnapshots_ProjectId_Day enforces idempotency
The daily job produces exactly one row per project per day, each carrying one count for backlog/plan/build/check/integrate/done

Shared attribution function is the single code path called by both the snapshot job and IssueQuerier.GetStageDurationsAsync (stage-duration), guaranteeing the two surfaces agree on an issue's latest stage

Attribution satisfies every spec scenario: backlog (no IssueWorkStarted as of day), done (terminal done as of day), in-flight (latest StageStarted as of day), cancelled excluded (reads com.mohist.issue.closed as of day)
Multi-run / rerun / rerun-from-stage / retry: the latest StageStarted as of day wins; the issue is counted once, never twice, in one stage
Re-running the job for the same project+day is idempotent: no duplicate row, counts unchanged (upsert via unique index)
No backfill: no snapshot row is persisted for any day before go-live; history accrues one day at a time

Job period is tunable (IOptions) and tests drive a sweep via the public SnapshotOnceAsync(CancellationToken) seam without ever starting the hosted loop or awaiting a wall-clock Task.Delay; time logic is injectable via TimeProvider
The job mutates no existing issue/session/workflow-run/approval domain state; the snapshot row is the only new write
npm test passes for the server (C# warnings-as-errors act as lint)
tasks.output: packages/server: shared attribution function, StagePopulationSnapshotRow + DbSet + migration, StagePopulationSnapshotService + registration, and unit/spec tests for attribution/idempotency/no-backfill
tasks.notes: Design D1 (job pattern), D2 (shared attribution), D3 (table shape), D4 (idempotent upsert), D5 (LINQ-to-objects day bounds + IssueClosed). Placement: job under Events/Hosting/, entity under Infrastructure/Data/StagePopulation/. Confirm the 90-day vs other window length is a read-endpoint concern (T-002); this task only persists counts.

tasks.title: Cumulative-flow additive read endpoint over a fixed trailing window
tasks.description: Add GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/issues/metrics/cumulative-flow, wired through IssueRoutes alongside MapIssueStageDurationMetrics so the existing ProjectResolutionEndpointFilter applies. The handler reads straight from the snapshot table (no event-stream recomputation) and returns CumulativeFlowResponse(Snapshots, RangeFrom, RangeTo) with CumulativeFlowDayDto(Day, Backlog, Plan, Build, Check, Integrate, Done), over a single fixed 90-day trailing window pinned as a constant (not caller-configurable). Time source is an injected TimeProvider.
acceptanceCriteria: 200 + ordered daily snapshots each carrying day + six per-stage counts for a project with snapshots within the window
200 + a defined empty series (Snapshots: []) when no snapshot has landed yet; never an error, never a fabricated snapshot
404 for an unknown/unresolvable project, produced by ProjectResolutionEndpointFilter before the handler runs
Trailing window is a single fixed 90-day constant and is not configurable by the caller
Strictly additive: stage-duration, delivery-time, cost, and all other existing project metrics endpoints remain available and unchanged
Handler reads only the snapshot table on the read path (no per-day recomputation from the event stream)
npm test passes for the server (C# warnings-as-errors)
tasks.output: packages/server: CumulativeFlowResponse/CumulativeFlowDayDto records, the cumulative-flow endpoint + IssueRoutes wiring, and endpoint tests (populated/empty/404/window)
tasks.notes: Design D6. Day/RangeFrom/RangeTo are 'yyyy-MM-dd' strings to match sibling metrics DTOs. 90-day window follows the design lean in Open Questions.

tasks.title: Dashboard stacked-area CFD widget in the Productivity zone
tasks.description: Add a useCumulativeFlow TanStack Query hook (fetchCumulativeFlow + cumulativeFlowQueryKey, staleTime 60_000, enabled on !!projectId, no refetchInterval) re-exported from entities/issue. Build a new AreaSeries stacked-area primitive in the chart kit (modeled on LineSeries's path approach, transform/opacity reveal gated by useReducedMotion). Implement CumulativeFlowChart.tsx following the 5-step sibling structure: useCumulativeFlow -> derive status via hasData guard -> section + ChartContainer three-state wrapper -> ChartAccessibility (SR summary + non-color legend) -> AreaSeries with one band per stage in workflow order, band width = that stage's daily count from the snapshot series. Mount it in ProductivityZone alongside the other flow charts.
acceptanceCriteria: One stacked band renders per workflow stage (backlog/plan/build/check/integrate/done) in workflow order; each band's width at a day encodes that stage's attributed count
Per-stage per-day band values come from the stage-population snapshot series; the widget performs no event-stream recomputation and introduces no new data-collection path

Loading, error, and empty states route through the shared ChartContainer three-state wrapper; the empty state names a concrete next action (CFD gains history once the first daily snapshot lands) and never renders a bare axis or fabricated bands
The six bands are distinguishable without color alone via legend shape/label + the screen-reader summary
Reuses the pinned chart baseline (theme-token fills, tabular-nums on numerics, transform-based motion honoring prefers-reduced-motion); no new charting library dependency is added
Widget is purely read-only: no writes to issue/session/workflow/approval state
npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web pass
tasks.output: packages/web: useCumulativeFlow hook + re-export, AreaSeries primitive, CumulativeFlowChart widget, ProductivityZone mount, and widget tests (band values/three-state/a11y)
tasks.notes: Design D7 (chart baseline composition) + D8 (six bands disambiguated by stacking order + legend shape/label, not hue; reuses fill-chart-1..5 by stratum). Update tests/setup.ts matchMedia stub if reduced-motion assertions require it.
